title: Consent-driven delta-propagation and safe-zone escape for analytics ingestion
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Problem: Console's analytics pipeline currently performs cross-region full replication of event streams for dashboards and billing. Several enterprise customers (and legal teams) require tenant-level consent boundaries and selective propagation of PII-linked events. We need a mechanism to (1) respect tenant consent and legal holds while minimizing replication surface, (2) allow a safe 'regional escape hatch' for emergency troubleshooting or legal requests that overrides standard residency rules but is auditable, and (3) reduce cost by shipping only delta changes for eligible tenants instead of full mirror sets. This ticket implements a consent-aware delta-propagation layer on the analytics ingest fanout and a guarded escape flow for emergency regional export.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline will micro-delta (event-level diffs) propagate only allowed event types to non-origin regions for tenants with explicit cross-region consent.
Tenants with no cross-region consent will not have PII-linked fields replicated; anonymized metrics and aggregated counters may be exported per config.
An auditable escape hatch exists: when invoked by authorized SRE/Security role, a timebound export to a target region may run with explicit log entries, reason, and approver recorded in audit log.
End-to-end integration tests prove that delta propagation reduces bandwidth by >= 60% for sample tenant workloads compared to full replication on the same window.
Console shows per-tenant residency status and last propagated delta watermark in the UI; alerts surface when delta lag > 30s or escape hatch used.
KMS-scoped keys used for region-targeted exports; usage is verified in staging with crypto audit flow.
tasks: Spec design: consent model extension (consent types, TTL, legal-hold override) - draft Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/consent-delta-propagation
Runtime change: add delta composer in ingest-proxy (continuous checkpointing, compacted change logs).
Routing: extend fanout-router to consult tenant consent registry and select delta vs full replication path.
Escape hatch service: implement guarded region-export endpoint behind RBAC + approval workflow; write to audit-log service.
Data transformation: add anonymization pipeline for blocked tenants (strip PII fields, produce aggregated metrics).
Observability: add per-tenant delta watermark metrics, replication bytes saved metric, and audit-hatch events to Console dashboards.
Tests: unit, integration, and chaos tests for partial network partitions and concurrent legal hold flips.
Docs & SDK: update ingestion docs, Console residency UI text, and runbook for SRE escape-hatch invocation.
architecture_decisions: Decision: Use compacted append-only change logs per tenant (LSM-style) to compute deltas; avoids expensive diffing of full datasets.
Decision: Consent registry stored in regional config-store with cross-region read replication; writes originate from control-plane and propagate via GRPC stream.

Decision: Escape hatch requires two-step approval: SRE initiates + Security/Risk TTL sign-off; implementation uses existing approval microservice (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/approvals/pull/412).
Trade-off: Delta propagation increases complexity of compaction and recovery; chosen because expected bandwidth/cost savings for multi-region customers justify operational cost.
Decision: Anonymization runs as a lightweight transformation stage (not full reprocessing) to keep latency under 200ms for streaming paths.
risks: Risk: Inconsistent state if compaction and delta checkpoints are lost during region failover. Mitigation: checkpoint replication + periodic tombstone reconciliation job.
Risk: Escape hatch misuse. Mitigation: RBAC, two-step approval, immutable audit entries, and automated post-hatch review reports.
Risk: Legal hold flips cause high re-sync load. Mitigation: backpressure and prioritized backfill windows with rate-limiting and cost-accounting tags.
Risk: Incorrect PII detection leading to leakage. Mitigation: conservative PII detection rules + manual allowlist + sampling-based QA.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement delta composer and consent registry; run synthetic tenants and validate delta volume reduction.
Phase 2 (canary): enable delta path for 5 low-risk tenants in us-west -> eu-west; monitor replication bytes and watermark lag for 72h.
Phase 3 (opt-in): expose tenant-level 'allowCrossRegionAnalytics' toggle in Console; offer migration utility to compute initial compaction snapshot.
Phase 4 (wider): enable for customers who opted in and verify billing metrics; enable anonymized exports for opt-out tenants where useful.
Emergency: escape hatch will be deployed behind feature-flag off by default; require Security opt-in before any customer can request usage.
test_plan: Unit tests for delta composer correctness and tombstone handling.
Integration tests: regional reader/writer pairs with network partitions simulated; verify watermark monotonicity.
Perf tests: measure bytes shipped and CPU overhead for delta vs full replication across representative tenant workloads.
Security test: run KMS key scoping and encryption verification; run SRE escape-hatch replay to validate audit logs.
E2E acceptance: create a demo customer, toggle consent, flip legal-hold, run escape hatch and verify audit entries + Console state.
